dedupe_keys.name: markov chain prediction of e bike availability and battery levels in barcelona s bicing system

description: This model, published as a 2024 preprint by Aleix Bassolas, Jordi Grau-Escolano and Julian Vicens of Eurecat, Centre Tecnològic de Catalunya, studies the battery levels of electric bikes in Barcelona's bike-sharing system, Bicing, and predicts both bike availability and battery levels with a Markov-chain approach. Coverage: Barcelona, using data supplied by the operator: 53 million trips from April 2019 to December 2022 (38% on e-bikes), battery snapshots every 8 hours through 2022, and snapshots every 30 minutes over three weeks from 29 March to 18 April 2023, with battery percentage, voltage, current, temperature, station, status and location. Bikes docked near the city centre rest for shorter periods and have lower average battery levels, which marks those neighbourhoods as vulnerable to depletion. Format and access: a preprint of 25 pages under CC BY 4.0. Licence and cost: the paper is free; the underlying data came from the operator and are not published with it. Caveats: one city and one operator; the code is not linked from the preprint. The approach can be used to add battery state to simulations of shared e-bike fleets and to plan charging and rebalancing operations. It relates to the FOMOsim micromobility simulator and the General Bikeshare Feed Specification in the catalogue.
